intent.raw_query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June from Chicago

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour
experiences.description: Wander through Rome's most charming medieval neighborhood sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artisanal cheeses, cured meats, and local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and market stalls. A guided tour brings the culinary history of the city to life.
experiences.location: Trastevere, right bank of the Tiber

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Experience
experiences.description: Discover Bernini's stunning baroque sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in this intimate villa gallery. Entry is strictly timed and limited to 360 visitors per session, creating an exclusive and unhurried art experience unlike any other in Rome.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration
experiences.description: Dive into Rome's authentic food culture at this beloved local market. Sample offal-based Roman street food, fresh pasta, seasonal produce, and artisan cheeses. Visit the nearby slaughterhouse-turned-contemporary-art-space MACRO Testaccio for a culture-food fusion experience.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit
experiences.description: Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire as golden hour light bathes millennia-old ruins in a warm glow. The Palatine Hill offers sweeping panoramic views over the Forum below, providing an unmatched blend of history, archaeology, and visual artistry.
experiences.location: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum, Historic Centre

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome (Georgia) airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Freshen up and get oriented in the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll around the local neighborhood near the hotel to get your bearings. Explore the nearby commercial strip along Turner McCall Blvd or Shorter Ave for a low-key first night. Window-shop and enjoy the warm June evening (expect highs around 30°C, so evenings will be pleasant).

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A near the hotel on Shorter Ave for a quick, budget-friendly first-night meal (~$8–12). Alternatively, grab groceries at a nearby Walmart or Kroger to stock up on snacks and breakfast items for the week.

day_by_day.notes: Since the hotel is in Rome, Georgia (USA) — not Rome, Italy — all itinerary activities are planned around the Rome, GA area and its surroundings. Confirm your transport from the airport to the hotel in advance. La Quinta offers free breakfast, so take advantage of it each morning to save on food costs. The weather will be warm (~30°C highs) with occasional rain, so pack light clothing and a compact umbrella.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy the free La Quinta breakfast at the hotel (saves $8–12). Then head to Myrtle Hill Cemetery (free admission), one of Rome's most iconic and scenic landmarks. Walk among the historic graves and enjoy panoramic views of the city and the confluence of the Etowah and Oostanaula Rivers forming the Coosa River. The hilltop setting is beautiful in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rome Area History Museum (admission ~$5) on Broad Street downtown to learn about the city's rich Civil War history, Cherokee heritage, and local culture. Afterward, stroll along Broad Street — Rome's charming main street — browsing local shops and admiring the historic architecture. Pop into any local art galleries or boutiques that catch your eye.
day_by_day.evening: Walk across the Oostanaula River and explore the River District. Enjoy the public art installations and murals along the riverfront (free). Watch the sunset over the river from the pedestrian bridge for a beautiful end to the day.

meals.breakfast: Free breakfast at La Quinta (eggs, waffles, coffee)
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Café on Broad Street — a local favorite with fresh, affordable sandwiches and salads (~$10–14). Ask for the daily special to save money.
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli on Broad Street — a Rome institution with hearty German-American deli sandwiches and plates at budget-friendly prices (~$10–15). Great local atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — downtown Rome is very walkable. Carry water as June afternoons can be hot and humid. Most downtown attractions are within a 1–2 mile radius, making this a very budget-friendly day with minimal transport costs.

day_by_day.morning: Free La Quinta breakfast, then drive or rideshare (~15 min) to Berry College — one of the most beautiful college campuses in the United States and the world's largest contiguous college campus. Admission is free. Explore the stunning Gothic architecture, rolling pastures, deer roaming freely, and the historic Ford Buildings. The campus is a genuine work of art in a natural setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Rome and visit the Chieftains Museum / Major Ridge Home (admission ~$5–8), a National Historic Landmark that tells the story of the Cherokee Nation and Major Ridge, a prominent Cherokee leader. The museum has fascinating art, artifacts, and cultural exhibits that connect art and history beautifully.
day_by_day.evening: Head back downtown for Rome's vibrant Friday evening scene. Check if there are any free outdoor concerts, farmers markets, or community events happening on Broad Street or at the amphitheater (Rome frequently hosts free Friday events in summer).

meals.breakfast: Free breakfast at La Quinta
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from Kroger or Publix and enjoy it on the beautiful Berry College campus grounds (~$5–7). Grab deli sandwiches, fruit, and drinks.
meals.dinner: El Sombrero Mexican Restaurant in Rome — generous portions of authentic Mexican food at very affordable prices (~$10–13). Great margaritas if you want to treat yourself on a Friday night.

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is a must-see — the grounds are stunning and completely free. Bring your camera. Check Berry College's website for any open campus events or art exhibitions in their galleries. If it rains in the afternoon (June averages 33mm), the Chieftains Museum makes a perfect indoor alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Free La Quinta breakfast, then visit the Rome Farmers Market (Saturday mornings, typically 8am–12pm) near downtown. Browse local produce, handmade crafts, local art, and artisan food products. This is a wonderful way to experience local culture and pick up affordable fresh snacks. Budget $5–10 for samples and small purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive approximately 45 minutes to Calhoun, Georgia to visit the New Echota State Historic Site (admission ~$7) — the former capital of the Cherokee Nation. The site features reconstructed buildings, a museum with impressive Cherokee art and cultural artifacts, and deeply moving historical exhibits. This is one of the most significant cultural and artistic heritage sites in the region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome and enjoy a relaxed Saturday evening. Walk along the Riverwalk trail along the Coosa River (free) as the temperature cools. Look for any live music at local bars or restaurants on Broad Street.

meals.breakfast: Free breakfast at La Quinta, plus fresh fruit or pastry from the Farmers Market
meals.lunch: Grab a budget lunch from the Farmers Market food vendors (~$7–10) or a local food truck. Fresh and local options abound on Saturday mornings.
meals.dinner: Applebee's or Cracker Barrel near the hotel for a reliable, budget-friendly dinner (~$12–16). Cracker Barrel is especially good value with large Southern-style portions.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the Farmers Market hours and location before going — times can shift seasonally. New Echota requires a short drive; consider carpooling or checking if a rideshare is cost-effective. The historic site is deeply moving and connects art, culture, and history in a powerful way.

day_by_day.morning: Free La Quinta breakfast, then spend the morning at the Coosa Valley Art Center or local galleries in downtown Rome (many are free or low-cost admission). Rome has a surprisingly active local arts scene. Check for any Sunday art exhibitions, open studios, or community art events happening this weekend.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive approximately 1 hour to Cartersville, Georgia to visit the Booth Western Art Museum (admission ~$10–12) — the largest permanent exhibition space for Western art in the eastern United States and a Smithsonian affiliate. The collection is world-class and covers cowboy art, Native American art, Civil War portraits, and Presidential galleries. Exceptional value for art lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome. Stop at a local grocery store to pick up ingredients for a simple in-room meal to save money after a day of driving, or grab takeout.

meals.breakfast: Free breakfast at La Quinta
meals.lunch: Dine at a local restaurant in Cartersville near the Booth Museum — Applebee's or a local diner for ~$10–13. Alternatively, pack a lunch from the hotel area before departing.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple in-room meal using a microwave (hotel rooms typically have one) — pick up rotisserie chicken, salad, and bread from Kroger (~$8–10 total). Great budget-saving strategy mid-trip.

day_by_day.notes: The Booth Western Art Museum is a hidden gem and a highlight for art lovers — absolutely worth the drive and admission cost. Check their website for any special Sunday programming or free admission days. Keep receipts for any museum admissions as some offer reciprocal benefits at other institutions.

day_by_day.morning: Free La Quinta breakfast, then explore Lock and Dam Park on the Coosa River (free admission) — a peaceful natural area with walking trails, river views, and picnic spots. Great for a morning walk in the cooler hours before the heat of the day sets in. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rome Little Theatre or check for any afternoon performances, art workshops, or community events happening in Rome. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at the Rome-Floyd County Library which often hosts free art exhibitions and cultural programming. Then revisit Broad Street for any shops or galleries you missed earlier in the week.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a nicer dinner as a mid-trip splurge — Rome has some excellent local restaurants that are still very affordable by most standards. Enjoy a leisurely dinner and reflect on the trip so far.

meals.breakfast: Free breakfast at La Quinta
meals.lunch: Subway or Jimmy John's near the hotel for a quick, cheap lunch (~$8–10) so you can maximize afternoon activity time.
meals.dinner: Pastime Restaurant on Broad Street — a beloved Rome institution serving classic American comfort food in a historic setting. Budget ~$15–20 for a satisfying dinner with local character. Try their famous pimento cheese or Southern-style entrées.

day_by_day.notes: Monday can be quieter for some attractions, so call ahead to confirm opening hours for any specific venues. The morning walk at Lock and Dam Park is best done before 10am to avoid peak heat. Stay hydrated throughout the day — June in Georgia is hot and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Final free La Quinta breakfast. Take a last morning walk through downtown Rome to soak in the atmosphere. Visit any shops you wanted to revisit for souvenirs — look for locally made art, pottery, or food products on Broad Street as meaningful, budget-friendly mementos. The Rome Area Council for the Arts may have affordable prints or local artwork for sale.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time before departure allows, make a final stop at Myrtle Hill Cemetery for one last panoramic view of Rome — a beautiful and free farewell to the city. Pack up, check out of the hotel, and head to the airport or onward destination. Allow extra time for check-out and transport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or travel to next destination. If your flight is in the evening, grab a final meal at a local spot near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Final free breakfast at La Quinta — stock up well for travel day
meals.lunch: Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A near the hotel for a quick, satisfying, budget-friendly farewell lunch (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Airport food or travel meal depending on departure time. If still in Rome in the evening, try Tijuana Joe's for affordable Mexican food (~$10–13).

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the week: By using the free La Quinta breakfast daily (saving ~$56–84 over 7 days), keeping lunches under $12, and mixing free attractions (Myrtle Hill, Berry College, Riverwalk, Lock and Dam Park) with low-cost paid ones (museums at $5–12 each), a comfortable 7-day trip is achievable for approximately $300–400 total in food and activities, excluding accommodation and transport. Rome, GA is a charming, underrated destination with genuine art, history, and food culture to explore.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Rome via Condor flight at 16:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit a nearby piazza or local shop to pick up essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first-night dinner close to the hotel. Explore a casual local trattoria within walking distance to ease into Roman cuisine without the pressure of a big outing after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit (grab a snack at the airport on arrival)
meals.dinner: Casual neighborhood trattoria near the hotel – try classic Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe or carbonara. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real – prioritize rest so you're energized for the full days ahead. Confirm any pre-booked experience tickets for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Start early (pre-booked timed entry recommended for 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections, from the Gallery of Maps to Raphael's Rooms, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and explore the Castel Sant'Angelo and the scenic Lungotevere riverside promenade. Rest in the shade during the hottest part of the day (around 2–3 PM, highs near 30°C). Browse the nearby Prati neighborhood for gelato and window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Prati neighborhood, a local favorite near the Vatican with excellent mid-range restaurants away from tourist traps.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café – cornetto and cappuccino, ~$8–12
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Vatican in Prati – try a Roman-style pizza al taglio (pizza by the slice) at a local bakery, ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Trattoria in Prati neighborhood – try saltimbocca alla romana or abbacchio (Roman lamb). Budget ~$25–35 per person with house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets well in advance online – they sell out weeks ahead, especially in June. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for the Sistine Chapel.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience: Book a timed entry slot (9:00 or 11:00 AM – mandatory, max 2 hours per visit). Discover Bernini's stunning baroque sculptures including Apollo and Daphne and The Rape of Proserpina, alongside Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in this intimate villa setting. One of Rome's most rewarding art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens – Rome's answer to Central Park. Walk or rent a rowboat on the small lake. Head down to the Spanish Steps and the Trevi Fountain area for sightseeing. Toss a coin and enjoy the baroque spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively streets around the Trevi Fountain and Via Veneto area for aperitivo hour (6–8 PM). Enjoy a Campari spritz or Aperol spritz with complimentary snacks at a bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel – cornetto, cappuccino, and fresh-squeezed orange juice, ~$8–12
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens – pick up supplies from a nearby deli (salumi, cheese, bread, fruit), ~$12–18
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near the Spanish Steps or Via Condotti – try Roman-Jewish cuisine like carciofi alla giudia (fried artichokes) and baccalà. Budget ~$30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be booked in advance at galleriaborghese.it – walk-ins are not accepted. Arrive 15 minutes early. The gallery limits visitors to 2 hours strictly.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration: Head to Rome's most authentic local food market (open until 2 PM, best visited 9–11 AM). Dive into Roman food culture by sampling offal-based Roman street food, fresh produce, artisan cheeses, cured meats, and local specialties. Chat with vendors and soak up the vibrant atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood – visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (where Keats and Shelley are buried), and the ancient Pyramid of Cestius nearby. Walk along the Aventine Hill to the famous Knights of Malta keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome, and visit the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Testaccio for dinner – this neighborhood is considered Rome's culinary heartland with some of the city's best value-for-money restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Testaccio Market itself – try supplì (fried rice balls), fresh pastries, and espresso from market vendors, ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Continue grazing at the market or grab a sandwich from a Testaccio deli – the neighborhood is famous for its porchetta sandwiches, ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Classic Roman trattoria in Testaccio – try rigatoni alla pajata or coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew). Budget ~$25–35 per person with local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is closed Sundays. Wear comfortable shoes – lots of walking on cobblestones. The Aventine Hill is a quieter, residential area – a lovely contrast to the tourist-heavy center.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Morning Visit: Arrive early (9:00 AM opening) to explore the ancient heart of the Roman Empire before the heat peaks. Walk through the Roman Forum among temples, arches, and basilicas, then climb Palatine Hill – the legendary birthplace of Rome – for sweeping views over the ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum (combined ticket with Forum/Palatine Hill). After the Colosseum, take a break from the heat in a nearby café or gelateria. Explore the Celio neighborhood and the beautiful Basilica of San Clemente – a fascinating multi-layered church with Roman ruins beneath.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour: Join an evening guided food tour through Rome's most charming medieval neighborhood (many tours depart around 6:00–6:30 PM). Sample supplì, artisan cheeses, cured meats, local wines, and tiramisu while wandering atmospheric cobblestone lanes.

meals.breakfast: Café near the Colosseum area – espresso and pastry, ~$8–10
meals.lunch: Trattoria in the Celio neighborhood near the Colosseum – try pasta all'amatriciana. Budget ~$18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour (multiple tastings). Supplement with a final glass of wine at a Trastevere wine bar afterward, ~$8–12 extra.

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum tickets online in advance – queues without tickets can be 2+ hours. The combined Forum/Palatine/Colosseum ticket is the best value. The Trastevere food tour should be pre-booked; check operators like Eating Italy or Walks of Italy.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic center on foot: Piazza Navona (Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers), the Pantheon (free entry, opens 9 AM – one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings), and the surrounding medieval streets. Spend 2–3 hours soaking in 2,000 years of layered history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Campo de' Fiori market (open until 2 PM on weekdays) for a browse, then explore the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood with its ancient ruins and unique Roman-Jewish heritage. Visit the Largo di Torre Argentina archaeological site (where Julius Caesar was assassinated) – now also a cat sanctuary. Rest during peak heat hours.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell splurge dinner at a well-regarded mid-range restaurant in the historic center or Trastevere. Enjoy a full Roman feast with antipasti, pasta, secondi, and dessert paired with a bottle of local Lazio wine.

meals.breakfast: Café near the Pantheon – try the famous Sant'Eustachio il Caffè for what many consider Rome's best espresso, ~$5–8
meals.lunch: Lunch at a trattoria in the Jewish Ghetto – try carciofi alla giudia and Jewish-Roman specialties. Budget ~$20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a quality Roman restaurant – budget ~$40–55 per person with wine. Consider making a reservation in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now charges a small admission fee (€5). Arrive early to avoid crowds. Sant'Eustachio il Caffè is a Rome institution – the coffee is served pre-sweetened by default, so specify if you want it without sugar.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – revisit a favorite spot or explore anything missed. Consider a peaceful visit to the Capitoline Museums (the world's oldest public museums, with stunning views of the Forum) or simply wander the streets of your favorite neighborhood one last time. Pick up last-minute souvenirs – artisan food products, local wine, or prints from street artists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a long, leisurely final Roman lunch. Pack bags, check out of the hotel, and transfer to the airport or onward destination.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or travel onward.

meals.breakfast: Final Italian breakfast at a neighborhood café – savor that last cornetto and cappuccino, ~$8–10
meals.lunch: Long, relaxed farewell lunch at a favorite trattoria discovered during the week – order something you haven't tried yet, like supplì, trippa alla romana, or a Roman-style seafood dish. Budget ~$25–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-transit dining (or early dinner before departure if schedule allows).

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer – Rome's Fiumicino (FCO) airport is about 45–60 minutes from the city center by train (Leonardo Express) or 60–90 minutes by taxi depending on traffic. Check out time is typically 11 AM – arrange luggage storage at the hotel if your flight is later.

day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the hotel's finest on-site dining option or a nearby upscale restaurant. Sip a welcome Aperol Spritz at the hotel bar, review the week's itinerary with your concierge, and retire early to prepare for a full first day.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: N/A – in-flight or airport meal
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at a premium local restaurant near the hotel – request the concierge to book a table at the best-rated fine-dining establishment within easy reach; opt for classic Roman pasta dishes such as Cacio e Pepe and a curated Italian wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real – prioritize rest. Confirm all upcoming experience bookings with the concierge this evening. Carry light layers as evenings can be breezy despite daytime highs near 30°C. June averages 33mm of rain so pack a compact umbrella.

Admire the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminate in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling before the crowds arrive. Dress code: covered shoulders and knees required.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and explore the elegant Prati neighborhood. Browse luxury boutiques along Via Cola di Rienzo, then visit Castel Sant'Angelo for panoramic rooftop views of Rome's skyline and the Tiber River in the warm afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour – As the heat subsides, join a premium small-group (or private) food and wine walking tour through Rome's most charming medieval neighborhood. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), artisanal cheeses, cured meats, and pair with local Frascati and natural Roman wines. End the evening with a digestivo at a candlelit Trastevere wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet featuring fresh pastries, Italian cold cuts, cheeses, seasonal fruit, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Il Sorpasso (Prati) – a beloved Roman bistro with an outstanding wine list and refined antipasti and pasta dishes.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour; supplement with a final dessert stop at a renowned gelateria such as Fatamorgana for artisan gelato.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican early-access tickets well in advance – they sell out months ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Stay hydrated in the June heat; carry a refillable water bottle (Rome's nasoni public fountains offer free cold drinking water throughout the city).

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience – Begin the morning with a timed-entry private guided visit to the Borghese Gallery, one of Rome's most intimate and spectacular museums. Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatically lit masterpieces. Entry is strictly limited to 2 hours, making it an exclusive and unhurried experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the lush Villa Borghese gardens – Rome's green lung – and rent a rowboat on the ornamental lake or enjoy a horse-drawn carriage ride. Descend to the Spanish Steps and explore the luxury shopping district along Via Condotti (Gucci, Bulgari, Valentino). Visit the Trevi Fountain in the mid-afternoon when light is ideal for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a premium dinner at one of Rome's celebrated fine-dining restaurants near the historic center. Consider La Pergola (Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel) for an unforgettable tasting menu with panoramic city views – book months in advance.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a classic Roman bar near the hotel – stand at the counter like a local for a cornetto (croissant) and a perfectly pulled double espresso.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch in Villa Borghese gardens: order a gourmet hamper from the hotel concierge or pick up premium provisions (prosciutto di Parma, burrata, truffle products, fine wine) from a nearby gourmet deli such as Roscioli Salumeria.
meals.dinner: La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri) – Chef Heinz Beck's three-Michelin-star tasting menu with optional wine pairing; one of Italy's finest dining experiences with sweeping panoramic views of Rome at night.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery requires advance booking – maximum 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. La Pergola reservations should be made months ahead. Dress code at La Pergola is smart elegant (jacket recommended for gentlemen). The gallery is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration – Dive deep into Rome's authentic food culture at the beloved Testaccio Market (Mercato di Testaccio), the city's premier local food market. Join a private culinary guide to sample offal-based Roman street food (supplì, porchetta, coda alla vaccinara), artisan cheeses, seasonal produce, and freshly baked bread. Learn about Roman culinary traditions from passionate local vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood on foot – visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (where Keats and Shelley are buried), the ancient Pyramid of Cestius, and the vibrant street art district of Ostiense. Cool off with a visit to a premium wine bar for an afternoon tasting of natural Italian wines.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit – As the golden hour light bathes millennia-old ruins in warm amber tones, take a private guided sunset tour of Palatine Hill and the Roman Forum. Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire with an expert archaeologist guide, enjoying the dramatic light and significantly reduced crowds compared to daytime visits.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast followed by early market snacking at Testaccio – the market experience itself serves as a progressive tasting breakfast/brunch.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) – a beloved Roman trattoria carved into Monte dei Cocci (a hill of ancient amphora shards) serving exceptional traditional Roman cuisine: rigatoni alla pajata, carciofi alla romana, and tiramisù.
meals.dinner: Post-sunset dinner at Aroma Restaurant (rooftop of Palazzo Manfredi) – a Michelin-starred restaurant with arguably the most spectacular direct view of the Colosseum in Rome; perfect for a magical evening meal.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is open Tuesday–Sunday, mornings only (closes around 14:00) – arrive by 09:00 for the best experience. The Roman Forum and Palatine Hill share a combined ticket with the Colosseum; book timed entry in advance. Sunset in Rome in June is around 20:30–21:00, making evening visits especially beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Pantheon (free entry on Sundays for EU citizens; small fee for others) with a private art historian guide who will illuminate its 2,000-year-old engineering marvel and artistic legacy. Afterward, wander the elegant Piazza Navona, admiring Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and the baroque church of Sant'Agnese in Agone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Doria Pamphilj Gallery – a hidden gem of Rome's private art collections housed in a magnificent baroque palazzo. Admire works by Velázquez, Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael in opulently frescoed rooms. Spend the later afternoon exploring the Campo de' Fiori market area and the Jewish Ghetto, one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhoods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a premium classical music concert – Rome offers world-class performances at venues such as the Auditorium Parco della Musica or intimate baroque church concerts (look for performances at Sant'Ignazio or the Oratorio del Gonfalone). Follow with a late Roman dinner in the Jewish Ghetto.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely Sunday breakfast at the hotel, followed by a coffee at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè near the Pantheon – widely considered Rome's finest espresso bar.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Il Pagliaccio (two Michelin stars, near Campo de' Fiori) – Chef Anthony Genovese's creative Italian cuisine with Asian influences; one of Rome's most innovative fine-dining experiences.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ba'Ghetto Milky (Jewish Ghetto) – an upscale kosher restaurant serving Roman-Jewish specialties: carciofi alla giudia (deep-fried artichokes), baccalà in tempura, and house-made desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday mornings in Rome are magical – many locals attend mass and the city feels quieter and more authentic. The Doria Pamphilj Gallery is often overlooked by tourists, making it a genuinely exclusive experience. Book concert tickets in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tivoli (45 minutes from Rome by private car): Visit Villa d'Este, a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its extraordinary Renaissance gardens filled with hundreds of fountains, water organs, and lush greenery – a refreshing escape from the city heat. A private guide will bring the history of Cardinal Ippolito II d'Este to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Villa Adriana (Hadrian's Villa) – the largest and most opulent villa ever built in the Roman world, spread across 120 hectares. Explore the emperor's private retreat with its Greek-inspired architecture, thermal baths, and serene reflecting pools with a knowledgeable archaeologist guide. Return to Rome by private car in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the rooftop bar of a luxury Rome hotel (such as the Minerva Roof Garden at Grand Hotel de la Minerve or the Stravinskij Bar at Hotel de Russie) for sweeping views of Rome's domes and rooftops at dusk. Follow with a celebratory dinner at one of Rome's iconic restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to Tivoli.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Sibilla in Tivoli – a historic restaurant (founded 1730) perched dramatically above the Temple of Vesta with stunning gorge views; serves refined Lazio regional cuisine.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Il Convivio Troiani (near Piazza Navona) – a long-standing Michelin-starred Roman institution with an exceptional wine cellar and refined contemporary Roman cuisine; perfect for a special evening.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Tivoli day trip for maximum comfort and flexibility. Both Villa d'Este and Villa Adriana require advance ticket booking. Wear sun protection and comfortable shoes – both sites involve extensive outdoor walking. Carry water as the June heat can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – revisit a favorite piazza or neighborhood at a leisurely pace. Consider a private cooking class or pasta-making workshop with a Roman chef (book through the hotel concierge) to take home authentic culinary skills as a lasting souvenir of the trip. Alternatively, visit the Capitoline Museums (the world's oldest public museums) for a final dose of Roman art and history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping along Via Condotti or Via del Babuino – pick up premium Italian leather goods, bespoke fragrances from Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella, or fine Italian wines and gourmet products from Enoteca Costantini or Roscioli. Return to hotel, pack, and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a beloved Roman restaurant to close the trip on a high note. Depart for the airport or onward destination by private luxury transfer.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent hotel breakfast – savor every last espresso and cornetto.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Roscioli Ristorante Salumeria (near Campo de' Fiori) – Rome's most celebrated deli-restaurant hybrid with an extraordinary selection of Italian cheeses, cured meats, pasta, and a legendary wine list of over 2,800 labels.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Osteria dell'Enoteca or a restaurant of choice selected with the concierge based on the week's culinary discoveries; focus on Roman classics: tonnarelli cacio e pepe, saltimbocca alla romana, and a final glass of aged Barolo.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your departure flight for airport transfer and check-in. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange a private luxury car transfer to the airport. Consider purchasing a curated selection of Italian wines, olive oils, or truffles from a gourmet shop as premium gifts or personal souvenirs – ensure they comply with airline liquid and customs regulations.
